officials.name: Aaron Tobias Polkey
officials.bio: As a fourth-generation peninsular Charlestonian proud of his Gullah Geechee heritage, Aaron Polkey is recognized as an inspirational leader, gifted communicator, and tireless advocate for historically marginalized individuals and communities. He serves as President & CEO of Palmetto Project, a statewide nonprofit organization, and previously worked as a Senior Program Attorney at Futures Without Violence. Polkey is an attorney who has advocated for affordable housing and equal voting rights.

officials.name: Boyd Gregg
officials.bio: Boyd was elected in January 2022 to serve as Councilmember for District 1. He is a licensed, professional engineer with Energy Systems Group, LLC, specializing in water resource recovery facilities. Boyd holds a B.S. and M.S. in Civil Engineering from Clemson University.

officials.name: Jim McBride
officials.bio: Jim was elected in November 2023 and sworn in as City Councilmember for District 3 in January 2024. He retired honorably from the U.S. Marine Corps as a Lieutenant Colonel after 25 years of active-duty service. Jim currently works for a remote patient monitoring technology company and lives on Johns Island with his wife, Lynn.

officials.name: Karl L. Brady, Jr.
officials.bio: Karl L. Brady, Jr. has served as the Charleston City Councilmember for District 5, representing Outer West Ashley, since 2019. He serves as Chair of the Ad Hoc Rules Committee and Special Facilities Committee, and Vice Chair of the Human Resources Committee and Traffic and Transportation Committee. Outside of City Council, Karl is the Director of Government Affairs for the Charleston Animal Society.

officials.name: Kevin Shealy
officials.bio: Kevin Shealy was elected District Two Councilmember in November of 2017. He is the owner and operator of the Kevin Shealy Insurance Agency, which supports hundreds of West Ashley families and businesses daily.

officials.name: Michael S. Seekings
officials.bio: Serving as Councilmember for District Eight is Michael S. Seekings, who was re-elected to his second term November 2017.

officials.name: Perry K. Waring
officials.bio: Representing District Seven is Councilmember Perry K. Waring, who was elected November 2011. He is a Financial Planner and holds a Bachelor of Science in Banking and Finance from the University of South Carolina (1977).

officials.name: Stephen Bowden
officials.bio: Stephen M. Bowden was elected to represent District 10 in November 2021. He graduated from Old Dominion University and the University of South Carolina School of Law. After a legal career representing homeowners, he joined the Charleston County Public Defender’s Office, where he also works with the Veteran’s Treatment Court.

officials.name: William P. Tinkler
officials.bio: William P. Tinkler won the election to represent District 9 in November 2023. He is a lifelong resident of and small business owner in West Ashley, and a graduate of Porter-Gaud School, Emory University, and the University of South Carolina School of Law. After law school, he worked as a staff attorney and law clerk before entering private practice, where he represents people and businesses in various legal matters.

officials.name: Teresa Wilson
officials.bio: As the City Manager of Columbia, South Carolina, Teresa Wilson stands as a transformative force, guiding the capital city toward a future defined by growth, innovation, and resilience. With a steadfast commitment to excellence, Wilson leads the city’s executive team, ensuring Columbia remains a vibrant, thriving community where residents and visitors alike can live, work, and play. Her leadership has been instrumental in driving Columbia’s development, prioritizing public safety, fostering economic growth, and improving the quality of life for all who call the city home.

officials.name: Brian Carnes
officials.bio: Brian is serving his fourth term on Lancaster County Council. He is a native of Indian Land and a graduate of Indian Land High School. Brian is a Partner and Chief Operating Officer of Carolina Innovations. He is an active member of Pleasant Hill United Methodist Church in Indian Land. Prior to being elected to Lancaster County Council, Brian served 8 years on the Lancaster County School Board (serving as secretary of the Board) and 4 years on the Pleasant Valley Fee Board (serving as chairmen for two years). He and his wife Pam have three sons, two daughters-in-law, and seven grandchildren.

officials.name: Charlene McGriff
officials.bio: Charlene McGriff has served three full terms on County Council representing District #2 and is beginning her fourth term. Ms. McGriff is a graduate of Brookstone College and attended USC-L, and is also a graduate of the Carolina Leadership Program. She has a long career in public service, including serving as Executive Director of Palmetto Citizens Against Sexual Assault since 1994 and 17 years on the Lancaster County School Board.

officials.name: Jose Luis
officials.bio: Jose brings over 22 years of experience in legal, operational, land acquisition, and development roles to Lancaster County Council. He has led organizations through significant growth and operational improvements, including a key role in the $10 billion merger of Family Dollar and Dollar Tree. The son of Cuban immigrants, Jose holds a BA from Florida State University and a JD from the University of Miami School of Law, and is married with two children.

officials.name: Steve Harper
officials.bio: Steve Harper is serving his fourth term on County Council representing District 5. He graduated from Lancaster High School in 1976. He graduated with a Bachelor of Science in Business Administration from the University of South Carolina in Columbia in 1981. He enjoys golf and supports the USC Gamecocks. He and his wife, Donna, have two sons, two daughters-in-law and four grandchildren.

officials.name: Stuart Graham
officials.bio: Stuart Graham is serving his first term on Lancaster County Council representing District 1. A lifelong Lancaster County resident, he has a background in finance and business management, and now works in his family's wedding/event venue and farm. He is actively involved in community leadership, including serving on the Van Wyck Town Council and the Lancaster County Capital Project Sales Tax Committee.

officials.name: Bryant Neal
officials.bio: Bryant Neal is serving his first term on County Council representing District 6. He is the owner of 521 Filling Station in Kershaw, SC. Bryant graduated from Andrew Jackson High School and The University of South Carolina at Lancaster. Bryant enjoys high school and college sports and is an active member of Center Grove Baptist Church where he serves as Chairman of Deacons. He and his wife, Beth, have two children, Laura Taylor (Reece) and Bry Neal (Abby), and two grandchildren, Annie Martin and Maes.

officials.name: Billy Mosteller
officials.bio: Billy Mosteller is serving his third term on Lancaster County Council representing District 3. He is owner of Mosteller Automotive & Alignment, LLC. He has been a volunteer fireman for 47 years and served 15 years as chief. He also served on the Lancaster County Fire Commission and the Lancaster County Sheriff's Office Advisory Council. He enjoys high school and college sports. He is a member of Hyde Park Baptist Church. Billy and his wife, Kathy, have a son, a daughter and four grandchildren.

officials.name: Will Haynie
officials.address: Town of Mount Pleasant Municipal Complex 100 Ann Edwards Lane Mount Pleasant, SC 29464
officials.bio: Council Member Will Haynie was elected to Council in November 2015. He was elected Mayor in November 2017 and re-elected in 2021. Born in Greenville, South Carolina, Mayor Haynie moved with his family to Mount Pleasant in 1966.

officials.name: Alex Crosby
officials.address: Town of Mount Pleasant Municipal Complex 100 Ann Edwards Lane Mount Pleasant, SC 29464
officials.bio: Alex Crosby is a longtime Mount Pleasant resident and a graduate of the University of South Carolina. A working mom raising her young family here, she is deeply rooted in the community. Alex helps run her family’s local insurance company, Crosby Insurance Group. She is active at St. Andrews Church, and is committed to serving her neighbors with transparency and respect. Outside of work, she enjoys learning about Mount Pleasant’s history and heritage, spending time on the water fishing, and exploring local parks with her son and their dogs. She also values staying active through hiking and yoga and appreciates any time spent outdoors with family and friends.

officials.name: Daniel Brownstein
officials.address: Town of Mount Pleasant Municipal Complex 100 Ann Edwards Lane Mount Pleasant, SC 29464
officials.bio: Daniel Brownstein was elected to Mount Pleasant Town Council on November 2023. Daniel, 44, is a married father of two who works as the marketing director at the law firm Rogers, Patrick, Westbrook & Brickman in Mount Pleasant. He has a Masters of Business Administration from the University of South Carolina and a bachelor’s degree in communication from Otterbein University.

officials.name: Howard Chapman
officials.address: Town of Mount Pleasant Municipal Complex 100 Ann Edwards Lane Mount Pleasant, SC 29464
officials.bio: Howard Chapman was elected to Mount Pleasant Town Council on November 2019. In 2025, he was elected to a two-year term as Mayor Pro Tem.

officials.name: Jake Rambo
officials.address: Town of Mount Pleasant Municipal Complex 100 Ann Edwards Lane Mount Pleasant, SC 29464
officials.bio: Jake Rambo was elected to Mount Pleasant Town Council in November 2019. Born and raised in Mount Pleasant, he holds degrees in education and leadership and has served as a teacher and principal before joining his family's business. He and his wife Sharon have three young children.

officials.name: John Iacofano
officials.address: Town of Mount Pleasant Municipal Complex 100 Ann Edwards Lane Mount Pleasant, SC 29464
officials.bio: Council Member John Iacofano was elected to the Mount Pleasant Town Council in November 2021 and leads with a philosophy centered on service, accountability, and meaningful results. As a long-time Mount Pleasant resident, John and his wife Krissy are raising their three children here. On Council, John has focused on strengthening partnerships in education, supporting public safety, and advancing a culture of professionalism within the Town.

officials.name: Kathryn Whitaker
officials.address: Town of Mount Pleasant Municipal Complex 100 Ann Edwards Lane Mount Pleasant, SC 29464
officials.bio: Kathryn Whitaker was elected to Mount Pleasant Town Council in November 2025. She served on the Town's Culture, Arts & Price Commission and was its Chair, working to make the Community Arts Center a reality. A South Carolina native, she is a successful business professional with over 20 years in legal marketing, and an active parent volunteer and church member.

officials.name: Laura Hyatt
officials.address: Town of Mount Pleasant Municipal Complex 100 Ann Edwards Lane Mount Pleasant, SC 29464
officials.bio: Laura Hyatt was elected to Mount Pleasant Town Council in November 2019. A Mount Pleasant native, she graduated from Wando High School and earned a pharmacy degree from the Medical University of South Carolina, working as a retail pharmacist for 30 years.

officials.name: A. Manning Lynch
officials.hours: Monday through Friday: 8 AM to 5 PM
officials.bio: A. Manning Lynch has served as Chairman of Spartanburg County Council since 2019. During his time on Council, he has also served as Chairman of Spartanburg Area Transportation System (SPATS).

officials.name: Bob Walker
officials.hours: Monday through Friday: 8 AM to 5 PM
officials.bio: Spartanburg County Councilman Bob Walker has spent much of his life in service for others. Born and raised in Landrum, Walker graduated from Landrum High School and the University of South Carolina before serving in the U. S. Air Force as a captain and pilot during the Vietnam War era. When Walker returned to Landrum in 1974, he joined First Baptist Church of Landrum and the Landrum Lions Club. For the past 40 years, he has served in many capacities in both the church and the Lions organization.

officials.name: Grant DeShields
officials.hours: Monday through Friday: 8 AM to 5 PM
officials.bio: Grant DeShields has lived in Spartanburg County his entire life and loves this community. He has been fortunate enough to work and raise his family in Spartanburg and wants to provide this same opportunity to others. Grant graduated from Byrnes High School and worked for his family’s business for 23 years.

officials.name: Jack A. Mabry
officials.hours: Monday through Friday: 8 AM to 5 PM
officials.bio: Jack is a lifelong resident of Spartanburg County and has proudly represented District 2 on County Council since 2018. He is the owner of Jack Mabry Allstate, where he has operated his business for more than 27 years. His record of public service includes 12 years.

officials.name: Jessica Coker, CPA
officials.bio: Jessica Coker, a native of Spartanburg County, is a self-employed CPA with 20 years of experience serving individuals and small businesses. She holds a Bachelors in Accounting and a Masters of Professional Accountancy in Taxation from Clemson. As an advocate for small business, her financial skillset is beneficial in her role as District 6 Representative.

officials.name: Monier “Mo” Abusaft
officials.bio: Monier “Mo” Abusaft is a graduate of Wofford College and Vanderbilt University Law School. At Wofford, his interest in ministry led him to graduate Phi Beta Kappa with a Bachelor of Arts in Religion. He was also awarded an ELI Fellowship, given to emerging leaders in ministry.

officials.name: Paul D. Abbott, Jr.
officials.hours: Monday through Friday: 8 AM to 5 PM
officials.bio: Paul D. Abbott, Jr. is a lifelong resident of Spartanburg County, a graduate of Cowpens High School, USC-Upstate, and Charlotte School of Law. He worked in his family businesses for approximately 30 years before becoming an attorney. He and his wife, Susan, live in the Hillcrest area and have six grandchildren.

officials.name: James T. McCain Jr.
officials.bio: James T. McCain, Jr., a native of Sumter, integrated the Sumter school system in 1965. After graduating from Morehouse College, he had a 35-year career in management with UPS. Upon retirement in 2009, he returned to Sumter and currently serves as Chairman of Sumter County Council.

officials.name: James (Jimmy) R. Byrd, Jr.
officials.bio: A lifelong resident of Sumter, South Carolina, Councilman Jimmy Byrd is the elected Council member for District #3 and currently serves as the Vice Chairman of Sumter County Council. He graduated from the University of South Carolina in 1997 with a Bachelor of Science Degree in Business Administration and was first elected to Sumter County Council on Dec. 19, 2006.

officials.name: Artie Baker
officials.bio: Arthur W. Baker, a member of Sumter County Council, was born on December 13, 1954, in Columbia, South Carolina. He is a 1973 graduate of Christ Church Episcopal School and received his Bachelor of Arts Degree in Health and Physical Education from Lander College in 1982, followed by a Masters of Education from the University of South Carolina in 1990. He was a teacher and coach in Sumter School District #2 and was first elected to Sumter County Council in November of 1994.

officials.name: Charles T. Edens
officials.bio: Charles T. Edens was born in Sumter, South Carolina, and is a graduate of Clemson University with B.A. and Master’s Degrees in Agriculture. Married with three children and four grandchildren, he has served on the Sumter County Council since 1999, completing certification courses for County Officials and graduating twice from the S.C. Economic Development School.

officials.name: Vivian Fleming-McGhaney
officials.bio: Mrs. Vivian Fleming-McGhaney holds a Bachelor of Science Degree from S.C. State University and two Master's Degrees in Education. She serves as the Coordinator of Curriculum and Instruction for Specialized Programs for Sumter County School District. Since 2002, she has been an elected member of Sumter County Council, representing District 5, and has served multiple terms as Chairman and Vice-Chairman.
